title: A beautiful AI mockup is not proof of readable contrast
summary: Measure a real pair of hex colours instead of trusting an accessible-looking image.

blocks.text: Do not judge text contrast from a generated screenshot alone. Antialiasing, gradients and guessed colours make visual inspection an unreliable substitute for measuring the actual foreground and background.

blocks.heading: A small test with real colours
blocks.text: Try gold #D4971B on cream #FDF7EE, white #FFFFFF on burgundy #7C1F16, and warm grey #84766A on cream #FDF7EE. Enter the actual hex pairs into the contrast calculator in the linked activity. Record the ratio and whether the pair meets the relevant threshold.

blocks.heading: Keep the thresholds separate
list: WCAG AA ordinary text generally needs 4.5:1.
Large text generally needs 3:1, using the standard size/weight definitions—not merely a large-looking screenshot.
A contrast pass alone is not a complete accessibility audit: keyboard use, names, structure, focus and other requirements remain.

blocks.heading: Make a change and test again
blocks.text: Choose one failing pair. Change the actual text colour or background in an editable heading or button, then recompute the ratio. Keep the before/after values and one remaining limitation. Do not declare the entire interface accessible from this single test.

blocks.heading: Try the full exercise
blocks.text: Open Practice is an independent, non-accredited collection of practical activities. The local calculator, fictional inputs and offline materials are free. An image generator is optional and its output is not an accessibility certificate.
